decision.top3_why: The mean of the full pool (strategy B) offers a stable, robust aggregation that aligns with the diagnosis of a trend‑dominated series and unstable model ranking. Its per‑window performance is consistently close to the best window (two windows identical at 0.6909) and only slightly lower on the third, indicating low variance. On the broader dataset, the mean strategy outperforms the median and is close to the weighted best, suggesting good generalization. The mean also benefits from the full pool, mitigating the risk of over‑reliance on any single model.
decision.top3_why_not: Candidate A (median) shows higher overall score but greater per‑window variance (0.7285 vs 0.6239 vs 0.7243) and is less consistent with the dataset’s preference for the mean. Candidate C (best_single) achieves the lowest validation score, but relies on a single model whose superiority varies across windows (CWT_rf only wins in window 0). With only three validation windows, the ranking is unstable and the single model may overfit, making it a risky choice for the blind test.

Its per‑window performance is consistently close to the best window (two windows identical at 0.6909) and only slightly lower on the third, indicating low variance. On the broader dataset, the mean strategy outperforms the median and is close to the weighted best, suggesting good generalization. The mean also benefits from the full pool, mitigating the risk of over‑reliance on any single model.
